doc.title: YGO Omega Troubleshooting Guide
doc.summary: Fix YGO Omega on Windows and Linux: updater errors, black screens, freezes, crashes on launch, Vulkan drivers, the 9999/9999 decks bug and Discord detection.

infobox.caption: YGO Omega, the free Yu-Gi-Oh! simulator by Duelists Unite

blocks.md:
This YGO Omega troubleshooting guide covers the problems players hit most often on **Windows** and **Linux**. Find your symptom below and jump to the fix. If you haven't installed the game yet, start with the [Install Guide](/wiki/omega-install-guide).

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| The updater downloads `update.zip` and stops | [Make the folder writable](#windows-updater) |
| The updater won't run on Windows 7 or 8 | [Move to a supported Windows](#windows-7-and-8) |
| Black screen on Windows | [Install codecs or reset](#windows-black-screen) |
| The game freezes on Windows | [Change the compatibility settings](#windows-freezing) |
| Stuck on the background picture | [Unblock GitLab](#windows-stuck-background) |
| `Segmentation fault` on Linux | [Check the drivers](#linux-crash) |
| 9999/9999 in the Deck Manager | [Install the SQLite packages](#linux-9999-decks) |
| Black screen on Linux | [Reset the settings](#linux-black-screen) |
| The game can't find Discord | [Replace snap or Flatpak Discord](#linux-discord) |

The folder you install to must be writable, or `OmegaUpdater.exe` fails. The game is portable, so you can move the folder later and it still works.

The easiest way is the [Windows installer](https://github.com/duelists-unite/omega-releases/releases/tag/Latest). It opens `OmegaUpdater.exe`, which downloads the game and its updates, then checks for missing .NET updates and firewall exceptions.

To install by hand instead:

1. Download `Omega_Launcher-Windows.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/duelists-unite/omega-releases/releases/tag/Latest).
2. Unzip it to a folder you have write permission for.
3. Run `OmegaUpdater.exe` and let it download the game.

If `update.zip` is left in the folder, the updater couldn't extract it. Follow the first fix below.

blocks.title: Unsafe file warning
blocks.md: The installer isn't code signed because signing is expensive, so Windows warns you that the file is unsafe. This is normal for unsigned programs, and the installer is safe to use.

blocks.text: The updater downloads update.zip but doesn't install it

blocks.md:
This is the most common case. The updater can download `update.zip` but has no permission to extract it over the game files, because the folder isn't writable.

1. Move the folder to the desktop, or right-click it, choose **Properties** and untick **Read-only**.
2. Press **OK** and run `OmegaUpdater.exe` again.

If it still fails, use the [Windows installer](https://github.com/duelists-unite/omega-releases/releases/tag/Latest).

blocks.text: The updater won't run on Windows 7 or 8

blocks.title: Windows 7 is not supported
blocks.md: The updater needs the latest .NET updates, and Microsoft no longer ships automatic updates for Windows 7 or 8. Upgrade to Windows 10 or later. Upgrading doesn't delete your files.

blocks.text: Black screen when you open the game

blocks.md:
Your system is missing the codecs that play video backgrounds. You have two options, and the first keeps animated backgrounds working.

1. Install the [K-Lite Codec Pack](https://www.codecguide.com/download_k-lite_codec_pack_full.htm).
2. Or open Command Prompt, go to the game folder and reset to static backgrounds:

blocks.code: "YGO Omega.exe" --reset

blocks.md:
Freezing comes from windowed mode, and it's an issue between Windows and Unity. Until there's a fix, use this workaround:

1. Right-click `YGO Omega.exe` and choose **Properties**.
2. Open the **Compatibility** tab.
3. Tick **Run this program in compatibility mode for** and pick **Windows 8**.
4. Tick **Disable fullscreen optimizations** and press **OK**.
If the game launches and never downloads any bundles, something may be blocking `gitlab.com`. Open `Player.log` in this folder and look for an error resolving GitLab:

blocks.code: %userprofile%\AppData\LocalLow\Duelists Unite\YGO Omega

blocks.md: If you use a custom DNS server or something like Pi-hole, whitelist GitLab and check that [gitlab.com](https://gitlab.com) opens in your browser. Then restart YGO Omega, and it should start downloading bundles.

Every distribution needs an up-to-date **Vulkan** API and **Kerberos 5**, which most distributions ship preinstalled. Some also need the **SQLite 3** development packages. Arch doesn't.

On Debian or Ubuntu:

blocks.code: sudo apt install libsqlite3-dev

blocks.md: On Fedora:

blocks.code: sudo dnf install sqlite-devel

blocks.md:
1. Download the [Linux launcher](https://github.com/duelists-unite/omega-releases/releases/download/Latest/Omega_Launcher-Linux.zip).
2. Make a folder for the game. Keep the name simple, like `ygomega`.
3. Extract the zip into that folder. From a terminal, install `unzip` first:

blocks.code:
sudo apt-get install unzip -y
unzip Omega_Launcher-Linux.zip

blocks.md:
4. Make `OmegaUpdater` executable: right-click it, open **Properties > Permissions** and tick **Allow executing file as program**.
5. Open a terminal in the same folder and run the updater, which downloads the game there:

blocks.code: ./OmegaUpdater

blocks.md: 6. When it finishes, make the game executable. Use the same right-click option, or run this in the folder:

blocks.code: chmod -R 755 .

blocks.md: 7. Double-click the game, or start it from the terminal:

blocks.code: ./YGO\ Omega

blocks.md: 8. Install [Discord](https://discord.com/) and leave it running, because the online servers need it. Use the version from Discord's site. [Snap and Flatpak builds don't work](#linux-discord).

blocks.text: The game crashes as soon as it launches

blocks.md: The game doesn't start at all, or the terminal ends with `Segmentation fault`:

blocks.code:
$ ./YGO\ Omega.x86_64
MemoryManager: Using 'Dynamic Heap' Allocator.

Set current directory to /home/fox/Omega
Found path: /home/fox/Omega/YGO Omega.x86_64
Loading in SingleInstance mode
Segmentation fault (core dumped)

blocks.md: This usually means the Vulkan drivers aren't set up properly. On AMD, it can also mean the `radeon` kernel driver is loaded instead of `amdgpu`.
Open a terminal with **Ctrl+Alt+T** and run:

blocks.code: lspci -nnk | grep -iA3 vga

00:01.0 VGA compatible controller [0300]: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. [AMD/ATI] Mullins [Radeon R4/R5 Graphics] [1002:9851] (rev 45)
        Subsystem: Dell Mullins [Radeon R4/R5 Graphics] [1028:06bf]
        Kernel driver in use: radeon
        Kernel modules: radeon, amdgpu
blocks.caption: radeon is in use, but amdgpu is available.

blocks.md: If your result looks like this, blacklist `radeon` and enable `amdgpu`:

blocks.code:
echo "blacklist radeon" | sudo tee --append /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist.conf
echo "options amdgpu si_support=1 cik_support=1" | sudo tee --append /etc/modprobe.d/amdgpu.conf

blocks.md: Then rebuild the initramfs for your distribution:

blocks.code:
# Debian and Ubuntu
sudo update-initramfs -u

# Fedora
sudo dracut -v -f

# Arch
sudo mkinitcpio -P

blocks.md: Reboot and run the `lspci` command again to confirm that `amdgpu` is loaded. If this doesn't apply to you, or the crash continues, set up Vulkan below.

blocks.code:
# AMD
sudo apt install libvulkan1 mesa-vulkan-drivers vulkan-tools

# NVIDIA
sudo apt install vulkan-tools

blocks.md: **AMD:** enable the repository, then install the Vulkan drivers.

blocks.code:
sudo add-apt-repository ppa:oibaf/graphics-drivers
sudo apt update
sudo apt upgrade
sudo apt install libvulkan1 mesa-vulkan-drivers vulkan-tools

blocks.md: **NVIDIA:** the drivers include Vulkan, so add the repository and install them.

blocks.code:
sudo add-apt-repository ppa:graphics-drivers/ppa
sudo apt update
sudo ubuntu-drivers autoinstall
sudo apt install vulkan-tools

blocks.md: **AMD:** Fedora ships the drivers out of the box, so at most you need an update.

blocks.code: sudo dnf install vulkan-loader mesa-vulkan-drivers vulkan-tools

blocks.md: **NVIDIA:** add the RPM Fusion repositories, which update themselves, then install the drivers.

blocks.code:
sudo dnf install https://mirrors.rpmfusion.org/free/fedora/rpmfusion-free-release-$(rpm -E %fedora).noarch.rpm https://mirrors.rpmfusion.org/nonfree/fedora/rpmfusion-nonfree-release-$(rpm -E %fedora).noarch.rpm
sudo dnf install xorg-x11-drv-nvidia akmod-nvidia vulkan-loader vulkan-tools

# AMD
sudo pacman -S vulkan-radeon lib32-vulkan-radeon

# NVIDIA
sudo pacman -S nvidia lib32-nvidia-utils

blocks.md: This command is the same on every distribution:

blocks.code: vulkaninfo | less

==========
VULKANINFO
==========

Vulkan Instance Version: 1.2.131


Instance Extensions: count = 18
====================
        VK_EXT_acquire_xlib_display            : extension revision 1
        VK_EXT_debug_report                    : extension revision 8
        VK_EXT_debug_utils                     : extension revision 1
        VK_KHR_surface                         : extension revision 25
blocks.caption: The start of a working result. The full output runs for pages.

blocks.md: If you see information like this, Vulkan is working.

The Deck Manager should list your own decks. If it fills with empty slots and shows **9999/9999** at the bottom, the SQLite 3 development packages are missing. Install them as in [Linux requirements](#linux-requirements), then reboot.

blocks.caption: A healthy Deck Manager, with one tile per deck

blocks.md: If the game never reaches the opening menu, it's trying to play an animated background your system doesn't support, which is a flaw in Unity on Linux. Run the game from a terminal with `--reset` to return to the default settings:

blocks.code: ./YGO\ Omega --reset

blocks.title: Animated backgrounds on Linux
blocks.md: Use `.webm` videos with the VP8 codec, and put a working video in the root of the `Backgrounds` folder. They use more CPU than `.mp4`, so keep them around 5 to 10 MB.

blocks.text: YGO Omega can't detect Discord on Linux

blocks.md: YGO Omega doesn't detect Discord installed from a **snap** or **Flatpak** package. Remove those first, as shown [below](#remove-snap-discord), then install a regular version for your distribution. Once you log in to Discord, you can open the game and go online.

blocks.text: Install Discord on Debian or Ubuntu

blocks.caption: Pick deb on Discord's download page

blocks.md:
Open [Discord's download page](https://discord.com/download), open the **Linux** menu and pick **deb**.

If you prefer the terminal, download the same file with `wget`:

blocks.code: wget -O discord.deb "https://discord.com/api/download?platform=linux&format=deb"

blocks.md: Either way, install the package from a terminal. Replace the path with the one to your `discord.deb`:

blocks.code: sudo dpkg -i /path/to/discord.deb

blocks.md: Discord comes from RPM Fusion, the same repositories as the NVIDIA drivers:

blocks.code:
sudo dnf install https://mirrors.rpmfusion.org/free/fedora/rpmfusion-free-release-$(rpm -E %fedora).noarch.rpm https://mirrors.rpmfusion.org/nonfree/fedora/rpmfusion-nonfree-release-$(rpm -E %fedora).noarch.rpm
sudo dnf install discord
sudo pacman -S discord

blocks.md: To install from the source instead, download the archive with `curl`, extract it and move it into place:

blocks.code:
curl -L "https://discord.com/api/download?platform=linux&format=tar.gz" --output discord.tar.gz
tar -xzvf discord.tar.gz
sudo mv Discord /usr/local/bin

blocks.md: List your snaps, then remove Discord. On Arch, the second command works without `sudo`. Fedora doesn't use snaps natively, so this shouldn't come up there.

blocks.code:
snap list
sudo snap remove discord
flatpak uninstall discord

items.q: Is the YGO Omega installer safe?
items.md: Yes. Windows warns you because the installer isn't code signed, which is normal for unsigned programs.

items.q: Does YGO Omega work on Windows 7?
items.md: No. The updater needs .NET updates that Windows 7 no longer receives, so upgrade to Windows 10 or later.

items.q: Why is YGO Omega a black screen?
items.md: The game can't play its video background. On Windows, install the [K-Lite Codec Pack](https://www.codecguide.com/download_k-lite_codec_pack_full.htm) or run the game with `--reset`. On Linux, run `./YGO\ Omega --reset`.

items.q: Why does YGO Omega crash on launch on Linux?
items.md: Usually the Vulkan drivers aren't set up, or an AMD system loaded the `radeon` driver instead of `amdgpu`. Follow [the crash fix](#linux-crash).

items.q: Why can't YGO Omega find Discord on Linux?
items.md: It doesn't detect snap or Flatpak Discord. Remove that version and install the one from Discord's site.

items.q: Where is the YGO Omega log file?
items.md: On Windows, `Player.log` is in `%userprofile%\AppData\LocalLow\Duelists Unite\YGO Omega`.

blocks.md:
Ask in the Omega-help channel on the [Duelists Unite Discord](https://discord.gg/duelistsunite). If a card behaves wrong, that's a bug rather than an install problem, so follow [Bug Reports](/wiki/bug-reports-how-to-report-a-ygo-omega-bug).

This page updates the [Installation and Troubleshooting Guide](https://forum.duelistsunite.org/t/installation-and-troubleshooting-guide/3802) by AntiMetaman on the Duelists Unite forum.
